narration.text: A distant star shines with a steady light.
Its planet is far too small and dim to see directly.
When the planet passes in front, it blocks a little starlight.
The star dims, just slightly, for a short while.
A larger planet blocks more light and makes a deeper dip.
The dip comes back each time the planet circles its star.

mustShow.text: a bright white star filling most of the frame, its glowing surface shimmering
a small dark round planet moving slowly across the bright glowing face of a star that fills the frame
a large dark round planet moving slowly across a wide part of the bright glowing face of a star that fills the frame

style.text: bright, well-exposed space imagery like a planetarium film: the subject is large, lit and moving from the first frame, warm glowing colours, slow continuous camera drift, no fade in from black

brief.title: A shadow in starlight
brief.summary: How a planet too small to see can be found by the tiny, repeating dip it makes in its star's light.
